title: Signal Fabric: Intake Lifecycle and Priority Gate for Tuning Requests (batching, KV cache, quant, routing)
creator: Ivy Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers and mid-market teams submit a mix of tuning and optimization requests (batching, prefix/KV cache, quantization profiles, routing policy changes). Current ad hoc intake results in slow TTR, inconsistent prioritization, and repeated handoffs between PM/Eng/SE. Goal: create a structured intake lifecycle (the 'signal fabric') that classifies signals, computes a reproducible priority score, and routes requests to one of three lanes: Auto-serve (self-serve guidance), Ops-Concierge (SE/PM assisted), or Eng-Work (engineering project). This ticket defines the PM playbook, scoring rules, required artifacts, SLAs, and handoff checks for the first pilot with three enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring rubric exists and is documented in Confluence with examples for common request types (batching, cache, quant, routing)

Intake form prototype implemented (CSV + web form) that collects mandatory signals: customer tier, traffic profile, tokens/sec, 95p latency SLO, current model and variant, current cost per 1M tokens, safety/regulatory constraints, and business outcome
Routing automation config in the PM-runbook that maps score bands to lanes and includes SLA targets: Auto-serve (48h), Ops-Concierge (5 business days), Eng-Work (SLO defined per project)
Pilot run completed with 3 enterprise customers; at least 60% of submitted requests are correctly auto-classified by score when evaluated by PM/SE retrospective
Clear artifact checklist for Eng-Work lane (PRD, perf traces, representative prompt set, reproducible benchmark script) and a QA gate defined
Stakeholder sign-off (PM, Solutions Eng, Eng Lead, Customer Success) recorded in the ticket comments
steps: 1) Finalize intake signal set and form fields (owner: PM)
2) Build a scoring rubric prototype in a spreadsheet and run it on last 120 historical requests to validate distribution (owner: PM + Data Analyst)
3) Define lane definitions, SLAs, and routing actions (auto-email to SE, auto-assign PM queue, create ENG-Work epic)
4) Implement light-weight web intake (internal) and CSV batch upload for partners (owner: Eng: intake-service backlog)
5) Pilot with three enterprise customers, collect feedback, measure match rate against manual triage (owner: Solutions Eng)
6) Iterate on rubric thresholds and publish playbook in Confluence; create template PRD and benchmark checklist
7) Hand off to Ops for production automation (incorporate into Console routing and Connectors roadmap)
scoring_formula: Score = (TierWeight * 0.35) + (CostSavingsEstimateNormalized * 0.25) + (SLORiskNormalized * 0.2) + (RepeatSignal * 0.1) + (RegulatoryFlag * 0.1). TierWeight: Enterprise=1.0, MidMarket=0.6, Startup=0.2. CostSavingsEstimateNormalized is percent tbps improvement from proposed knobs normalized to 0..1. SLORiskNormalized is severity of current SLO breaches (0..1). RepeatSignal is 1 if similar request from same customer in last 60 days. RegulatoryFlag is 1 if PII/compliance constraints present (forces higher priority). Score bands: 0-0.35=Auto-serve, 0.35-0.7=Ops-Concierge, 0.7-1.0=Eng-Work.
risks: Under-specified signals lead to misclassification (false negatives)
Engineering capacity may not match Eng-Work demand; need clear admission control
Customers may expect faster times than SLAs for high-value accounts; require override policy and audit trail
dependencies_notes: Relies on ENG-2083 (intake-service API) for web form and on PM-34277 for prior lane definitions; data analyst access to historical request dataset required (ticket opened)
